question: What exactly is salpingitis?

options.A: Bacterial colonization of the outer vulva
options.B: Malignant growth inside the uterine muscle wall
options.C: Fungal overgrowth within the vaginal vault
options.D: Infection and inflammation of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Salpingitis simply means inflammation in the fallopian tubes, usually caused by bacteria moving up from the lower reproductive tract. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h1)

question: Why are fallopian tubes easily reached by infections starting in the lower vagina or cervix?

options.A: They lack any blood supply to fight off invading microorganisms
options.B: They produce constant secretions that feed bacterial pathogens
options.C: They share a continuous open mucosal pathway with the uterus and cervix
options.D: They are located outside the main pelvic cavity entirely

explanation: Because the female reproductive tract is an open road from the vagina up through the uterus and tubes, bacteria can easily travel upward. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h1)

question: Which two common bacteria are most often responsible for causing salpingitis?
explanation: Chlamydia and gonorrhea are the sexually transmitted bacteria behind the vast majority of acute salpingitis cases. Great to keep in mind for clinical practice! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h2)

question: A young female patient asks how she got a fallopian tube infection when she felt fine down below. What is the most likely reason?

options.A: A sudden genetic mutation in her uterine lining cells
options.B: An asymptomatic ascending sexually transmitted infection like chlamydia
options.C: A severe allergic reaction to standard hormonal contraceptives
options.D: Eating contaminated food that spread bacteria to her pelvis

explanation: Chlamydia is famous for being silent at first in the lower tract, quietly creeping upward before causing noticeable pain in the tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h2)

question: What change typically happens inside the fallopian tubes after a severe infection heals?

options.A: Replacement of tubal tissue with normal ovarian follicles
options.B: Complete regeneration of healthy, unimpeded mucosal cilia
options.C: Permanent widening and increased muscular strength of the walls
options.D: Fibrous scar bands and adhesions that obstruct the lumen

explanation: Just like a skin wound leaves a scar, healing inside the delicate tubes creates fibrous bands that can narrow or block the passage. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h3)

question: What pocket of pus can develop near the fallopian tube and ovary during a bad pelvic infection?
explanation: When upper reproductive infections get severe, pus can collect and form a painful pocket involving both the tube and the ovary, called a tubo-ovarian abscess. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h3)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of acute salpingitis?

options.A: Sharp pain located exclusively in the upper right shoulder
options.B: Bilateral lower abdominal and pelvic pain
options.C: Severe itching of the external perineal skin
options.D: Painless swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: Since both tubes can be affected, inflammation usually shows up as lower belly or pelvic pain felt on both sides. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h4)

question: Why might a patient with salpingitis feel deep pelvic pain during sexual intercourse?

options.A: Vaginal contractions trap air inside the closed uterine cavity
options.B: Hormonal shifts completely stop natural vaginal lubrication
options.C: Pelvic thrusting puts pressure on inflamed, swollen fallopian tubes and surrounding tissues
options.D: The infection causes immediate dryness of the external labial skin

explanation: Movement during sex jostles the pelvic organs, which hurts when the tubes are already swollen, tender, and inflamed. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h4)

question: During a pelvic exam, what specific finding strongly points toward a condition like salpingitis?

options.A: Hyperactive bowel sounds in all four quadrants
options.B: Complete absence of deep tendon reflexes

explanation: Cervical motion tenderness happens when moving the cervix causes sudden, sharp pain because the inflamed pelvic organs right above it are disturbed. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h5)

question: Why is a pregnancy test almost always ordered when a patient arrives with lower belly pain and suspected salpingitis?

options.A: To confirm that the patient is currently using hormonal contraceptives
options.B: To rule out an ectopic pregnancy, which can present with similar pain
options.C: To measure baseline kidney function before starting antibiotic therapy
options.D: To check if high hormone levels caused the bacterial overgrowth

explanation: An ectopic pregnancy is a medical emergency that can mimic pelvic infection pain, so nurses always check this first to keep the patient safe. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h5)

question: Why must the sexual partner of someone treated for salpingitis also get antibiotic treatment?

options.A: To balance the hormonal levels of both partners concurrently
options.B: To prevent reinfection of the patient and stop further community spread
options.C: To ensure the male partner does not develop a bladder infection
options.D: To satisfy mandatory legal reporting requirements for minor illnesses

explanation: Treating both partners breaks the ping-pong cycle of passing the STI back and forth. Teamwork in healthcare matters! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h6)

question: A patient with severe salpingitis, high fever, and nonstop vomiting is admitted for IV antibiotics. What is the main reason for hospital admission?

options.A: Need for immediate total removal of both fallopian tubes
options.B: Requirement for daily pelvic ultrasound monitoring at bedside
options.C: Desire to isolate the patient from all household family members
options.D: Inability to tolerate oral medications due to severe nausea

explanation: If a patient can't keep pills down because of vomiting, oral meds won't work. Bringing them in for IV treatment ensures the drugs actually get into their system. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h6)

question: What is the most crucial piece of advice for a patient sent home with a 14-day course of antibiotics for salpingitis?

options.A: Save half the pills in case the infection returns next month
options.B: Double the dose if you miss a pill during the middle of the week
options.C: Stop taking the medication as soon as your pelvic pain goes away
options.D: Finish every single pill, even if you start feeling completely better

explanation: Feeling better doesn't mean all germs are gone. Stopping early can let tougher bacteria survive and bring the infection right back. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h7)

question: A patient asks when she can safely have sexual intercourse again after treatment. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Wait until you and your partner have finished all medications and symptoms are completely gone
options.B: Wait at least six full months regardless of how you feel physically
options.C: Intercourse is completely safe once you have taken your first dose of antibiotics
options.D: You can resume intercourse as soon as your pelvic pain drops below a mild level

explanation: Waiting until both partners finish their meds ensures everyone is healed and prevents an instant reinfection. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h7)

question: How does severe scarring from past salpingitis increase the risk of an ectopic pregnancy?

options.A: Fibrous bands force the ovaries to release eggs directly into the peritoneal cavity
options.B: Scar tissue blocks the fertilized egg from traveling down to the uterus, causing it to implant in the tube
options.C: Adhesions destroy all hormonal production needed to support a normal pregnancy
options.D: Scars cause the uterus to shrink so much that eggs refuse to enter it

explanation: When scar tissue narrows or blocks the tube, a fertilized egg gets stuck and has to try to grow right there in the tube instead of the uterus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h8)

question: Which of the following is a well-known long-term reproductive complication of untreated salpingitis?
explanation: Tubal scarring can block the path entirely, making it very difficult for sperm and egg to meet, which can lead to fertility challenges. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h8)
